## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raja_Ravi_Varma&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Raja Ravi Varma is sometimes regarded as the first modern Indian artist due to his ability to reconcile Western aesthetics with Indian iconography. The Indian art historian and critic [Geeta Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geeta_Kapur "Geeta Kapur") wrote,

> Ravi Varma is the indisputable father figure of modern Indian art. Naive and ambitious at the same time, he opens up the debate for his later compatriots in the specific matter of defining individual genius through professional acumen, of testing modes of cultural adaptation with idiosyncratic effect, of attempting pictorial narration with its historic scope.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-15)

Similarly, Baroda School artist [Gulam Mohammed Sheikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulam_Mohammed_Sheikh "Gulam Mohammed Sheikh") also wrote about Ravi Varma as a modern artist. In his essay "Ravi Varma in Baroda", Sheikh asserted that Varma was a key figure in the establishment of Indian modern art, claiming that "the story of contemporary Indian art was never the same after Ravi Varma had entered it. He left his imprint on almost every aspect of it." Like Kapur, Sheikh praised Ravi Varma's integration of Indian and Western aesthetics and techniques, comparing him favorably to Indian modernist [Nandalal Bose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandalal_Bose "Nandalal Bose").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-16)

However, Ravi Varma's legacy is controversial. Fellow Baroda School artist and art historian [Ratan Parimoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratan_Parimoo "Ratan Parimoo") saw Ravi Varma in a less favorable light, derogatorily referring to him as [kitsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitsch "Kitsch") and claiming Varma's work was less spiritually authentic than folk art and tribal art. He argued that Ravi Varma was responsible for the "vulgarity" of popular art, comparing Varma's work to the lurid colors and sexuality of popular images in [calendar art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calendar_art?action=edit&redlink=1 "Calendar art (page does not exist)") and films.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-18) Australian art critic [Christopher Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Allen_(critic) "Christopher Allen (critic)") made the same points in his review of the 2026 exhibition _The God of Small Things: Faith and Popular Culture_ at the [Queensland Art Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland_Art_Gallery "Queensland Art Gallery").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-19)

Despite his controversial legacy, Ravi Varma continues to be an important figure for modern and contemporary Indian artists. For example, modern artist [Nalini Malani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nalini_Malani "Nalini Malani") recreated Ravi Varma's _[Galaxy of Musicians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaxy\_of\_Musicians "Galaxy of Musicians")_ in her video installation _Unity in Diversity_ to interrogate Ravi Varma's idealistic nationalism.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-20) Similarly, contemporary artist [Pushpamala N.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pushpamala_N. "Pushpamala N.") recreated several Ravi Varma paintings with herself as the subject to deconstruct Ravi Varma's idealized depictions of goddesses and Indian women.

Many organizations do programs in his memory and give awards in his name. A two days festival of The Maharaja Ranjitsinh Gaekwad Festival of Arts is annually organized, in his memory at the [Durbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durbar_(court) "Durbar (court)") Hall in [Laxmi Vilas Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmi_Vilas_Palace "Laxmi Vilas Palace"), [Vadodara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadodara "Vadodara"), [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-Sandesh2022-22) The Raja Ravi Varma Award for Excellence in the Field of Visual Arts is presented during this festival. [Jayant Parikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayant_Parikh "Jayant Parikh") was the first recipient.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-24)

## In popular culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raja_Ravi_Varma&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: In popular culture")]

[J. Sasikumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Sasikumar "J. Sasikumar") made _Raja Ravi Varma_, an Indian documentary television film on the artist in 1997. It was produced by the [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India")'s [Films Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Films_Division_of_India "Films Division of India").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-30)

_[Makaramanju](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makaramanju "Makaramanju")_ (English: _The Mist of Capricorn_) is a 2011 Indian [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam")-language romantic drama film by [Lenin Rajendran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenin_Rajendran "Lenin Rajendran") starring [Santosh Sivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santosh_Sivan "Santosh Sivan") as Varma, the film focuses on Varma's painting "Urvashi Pururavas".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-31) The 2014 Indian Hindi-language film, _[Rang Rasiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rang\_Rasiya "Rang Rasiya")_ (English title: _Colours of Passion_) explores Varma's inspiration behind his paintings with [Randeep Hooda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randeep_Hooda "Randeep Hooda") in the role of the painter.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-hooda_paint-32)

**Thiruvananthapuram** (Malayalam pronunciation:[[t̪iɾuʋənən̪d̪ɐˈbuɾəm]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/b/b9/Trivandrum.ogg/Trivandrum.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Trivandrum.ogg "File:Trivandrum.ogg")[_tirr-ROO-və-nun-Tə-poor-əm_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")), also known as **Trivandrum**, is the [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_city "Capital city") city of the Indian state of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-10) As of 2011, the [Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Municipal_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation") had a population of 957,730 over an area of 214.86 km 2,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-citypop-11) making it the most populous city in Kerala.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-districtprofile-12) The larger [Thiruvananthapuram metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_metropolitan_area "Thiruvananthapuram metropolitan area") has over 1.7 million inhabitants within an area of 543 km 2, making it the second-most populous [metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area") in Kerala after [Kochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi_metropolitan_area "Kochi metropolitan area").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-uapop-13) Thiruvananthapuram is one of the few cities in India that serves as a state capital and is also centre for heritage, maritime activities, information technology, research and development, space research, defence, automotive technology, and biosciences. It is also among the few cities in the world where both an [international airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum_International_Airport "Trivandrum International Airport") and an [international seaport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vizhinjam_International_Seaport_Thiruvananthapuram "Vizhinjam International Seaport Thiruvananthapuram") are located within the city in close proximity to the city center.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-14)

Located on the west coast of India near the extreme south of the mainland, Thiruvananthapuram is a port city located 10 [nautical miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile "Nautical mile") (19 km; 12 mi)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-15) from a heavily trafficked east–west shipping channel. The city is home to India's first deep-water trans-shipment port, the [Vizhinjam International Seaport Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vizhinjam_International_Seaport_Thiruvananthapuram "Vizhinjam International Seaport Thiruvananthapuram").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-16) The city is characterised by its undulating terrain of low coastal hills.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-17) Thiruvananthapuram is also known for its cultural heritage, being associated with the musical contributions of [Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swathi_Thirunal "Swathi Thirunal") and the artistic legacy of painter Raja Ravi Varma. Thiruvananthapuram has contributed to the development of [Malayalam literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_literature "Malayalam literature") through individuals like [Ulloor S. Parameswara Iyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulloor_S._Parameswara_Iyer "Ulloor S. Parameswara Iyer"), [Kumaran Asan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumaran_Asan "Kumaran Asan"), [C. V. Raman Pillai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._V._Raman_Pillai "C. V. Raman Pillai") and [Narayana Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narayana_Guru "Narayana Guru"). The city is also known for [Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Padmanabhaswamy_Temple "Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple"), known as the richest temple in the world.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-18) The other temples includes the Sreevaraham temple, the Shreekanteswaram temple and the Attukal Bhagavathy temple.

The present regions that constitute Thiruvananthapuram were ruled by the [Ays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_kingdom "Ay kingdom") who were related to feudatories of the [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19) In the 12th century, it was conquered by the [Kingdom of Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19) In the 18th century, the king [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_varma "Marthanda varma") expanded the territory, founded the princely state of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") and made Thiruvananthapuram its capital.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-history1-20)[Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") became the most dominant state in Kerala by defeating the powerful [Zamorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamorin "Zamorin") of [Calicut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Calicut "History of Calicut") in the battle of [Purakkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purakkad "Purakkad") in 1755.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-AHoT_162-21) Following [India's independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement") in 1947, Thiruvananthapuram became the capital of [Travancore–Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore%E2%80%93Cochin "Travancore–Cochin") state and remained so until the new Indian state of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") was formed in 1956.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-23)

Thiruvananthapuram is a notable academic and research hub and home to the [University of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kerala "University of Kerala"), [APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APJ_Abdul_Kalam_Technological_University "APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University"), the regional headquarters of [Indira Gandhi National Open University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi_National_Open_University "Indira Gandhi National Open University"), and many other schools and colleges. Thiruvananthapuram is also home to research centres such as the [National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_for_Interdisciplinary_Science_and_Technology "National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology"), [Indian Space Research Organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Space_Research_Organisation "Indian Space Research Organisation")'s [Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikram_Sarabhai_Space_Centre "Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre"), the [Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Space_Science_and_Technology "Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology"), [National Centre for Earth Science Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Centre_for_Earth_Science_Studies "National Centre for Earth Science Studies") and a campus of the [Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institutes_of_Science_Education_and_Research "Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-24) Thiruvananthapuram is where India's space program began, with the headquarters of [Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Propulsion_Systems_Centre "Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre") located there. The city is home to media institutions like [Toonz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toonz "Toonz") Animation India and [Tata Elxsi Ltd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tata_Elxsi "Tata Elxsi"), and also to [Chitranjali Film Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitranjali_Studio "Chitranjali Studio"), one of the first film studios in [Malayalam Cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_Cinema "Malayalam Cinema"), and [Kinfra Film and Video Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinfra_Film_and_Video_Park "Kinfra Film and Video Park") at [Kazhakoottam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakoottam "Kazhakoottam"), which is India's first infotainment industrial park.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-25)

In 2012, Thiruvananthapuram was named the best Kerala city to live in, by a field survey conducted by _[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-26) In 2013, the city was ranked the fifteenth best city to live in India, in a survey conducted by _[India Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India\_Today "India Today")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-India_Today_survey-27) Thiruvananthapuram was ranked the best Indian city for two consecutive years, 2015 and 2016, according to the Annual Survey of India's City-Systems (ASICS) conducted by the [Janaagraha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janaagraha "Janaagraha") Centre for Citizenship and Democracy.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Best_Indian_City-28) The city was also selected as the best governed city in India in a survey conducted by Janaagraha Centre for citizenship and democracy in 2017.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Best_Governed_City-29)

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

The city takes its name from the [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam") word _thiru-anantha-puram_ (തിരുവനന്തപുരം[[t̪iɾuʋɐnɐn̪d̪ɐpuɾɐm]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/8/86/En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga/En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga "File:En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga")), meaning "The City of Lord Anantha (means infinite, endless, or eternal)",[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Meaning_of_name-30) referring to the [deity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deity "Deity") of the [Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Padmanabhaswamy_Temple "Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple") located in the city. Thiruvananthapuram is also known in literature, and popular reference as _Ananthapuri_, derived from the [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") word _Syanandurapuram_, meaning "The City of Bliss" in Carnatic [kirtanas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirtan "Kirtan") composed by [Swathi Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swathi_Thirunal "Swathi Thirunal"), erstwhile Maharaja of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-31) The city was officially referred to as _Trivandrum_ until 1991 (Trivandrum being the anglicised name of the town), when the government decided to reinstate the city's original name Thiruvananthapuram. Many Malayalees still refer to the city as Trivandrum, however.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-32) The city was also called as _Anandapatnam_ or _Anandapatam_ in [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") and [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") languages meaning "The City of Ananda" which is the same to meaning for the original name. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Pre Historic Period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Pre Historic Period")]

Thiruvananthapuram is a relatively modern region with trading traditions dating back to 1000 BCE.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-34) It is believed that the ships of [King Solomon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon "Solomon") landed in a port then called [Ophir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ophir "Ophir") (now [Poovar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poovar "Poovar")) in Thiruvananthapuram in 1036 BCE.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-36) The city was the trading post of [spices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spices "Spices"), [sandalwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandalwood "Sandalwood") and [ivory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivory "Ivory").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Ancient_Trade_in_Thiruvananthapuram-37) However, the ancient political and cultural history of the city was almost entirely independent from that of the rest of Kerala. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Ancient Period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Ancient Period")]

The southern region of present-day Kerala state (The coastal belt between Thiruvananthapuram and [Alappuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alappuzha "Alappuzha")) was under [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty"), which was more related to the [Pandya dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty") of [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai "Madurai").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-38)[_[page needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_] The early rulers of the city were the [Ays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_kingdom "Ay kingdom"). [Vizhinjam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vizhinjam "Vizhinjam"), which is now a region in the present-day Thiruvananthapuram, was the capital of the [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-39) Vizhinjam was an important port city from as early as the second century BC.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-41) During the Ay dynasty's rule, Thiruvananthapuram witnessed many battles in which the [Chola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty") and [Pandyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandyan_dynasty "Pandyan dynasty") dynasties attempted to capture the port town.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis1-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis2-43)

### Middle Ages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Middle Ages")]

After the death of king [Vikramaditya Varaguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikramaditya_Varaguna "Vikramaditya Varaguna") in 925 AD, the glory of the Ays departed and almost all their territories became part of the [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-44)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19) During the tenth century, the Cholas attacked and sacked Vizhinjam and surrounding regions.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19) The port in Vizhinjam and the historic education center of Kanthalloor Sala were also destroyed by Cholas during this period.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-kanthalloor-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-46) A branch of the Ay family, which had controlled the [Padmanabhaswamy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmanabhaswamy_Temple "Padmanabhaswamy Temple"), merged with the [Kingdom of Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad") in the 12th century.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19)

A map of [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") drawn by Homann Heirs in 1733. At that time, Travancore was only a small territory wedged between [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam") and [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari"), as shown in the map (Present-day districts of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district") and Kanyakumari only). 

### Early Modern Period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Early Modern Period")]

 It was in the later half of the 18th century, that Travancore inherited the kingdoms up to [Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin") and became a powerful kingdom, and Thiruvananthapuram became a major city of Kerala.

Present-day Thiruvananthapuram city, district, and [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"), were parts of the [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty") during ancient and [medieval ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"), in the southernmost part of the Indian subcontinent.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-askh-47) Ay kingdom had experienced attacks and conquests by [Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty") and [Pandyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty") in various periods.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-askh-47) Later it became a part of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad") in late Middle Ages, which was eventually expanded as the powerful kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") in the 18th century CE.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-askh-47) The [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_people "Tamil people")-Dravidian kind of architecture is also found in Padmanabhaswamy temple, which makes it distinct and unique from the architectural style of temples in northern and central parts of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-askh-47)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Thambiran_Vanakkam_1578.JPG/250px-Thambiran_Vanakkam_1578.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Thambiran_Vanakkam_1578.JPG)

_[Thambiran Vanakkam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thambiran\_Vanakkam "Thambiran Vanakkam")_ was printed at Kollam, the capital of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad") in 1578, during the Portuguese Era. It holds the record of the first book printed in any Indian language. It was written in the language _[Lingua Malabar Tamul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingua\_Malabar\_Tamul "Lingua Malabar Tamul")_ which was spoken in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") during the medieval period.

### Late Modern Period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Late Modern Period")]

In the early 18th century CE, the [Travancore royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore_royal_family "Travancore royal family") adopted some members from the royal family of [Kolathunadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolathunadu "Kolathunadu") based at [Kannur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannur "Kannur").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-48) Then, [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma") who inherited the Kingdom of Venad expanded the kingdom by conquering the kingdoms of [Kayamkulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kayamkulam "Kayamkulam"), [Kottarakkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottarakkara "Kottarakkara"), [Kottayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kottayam "Kottayam"), [Changanassery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changanassery "Changanassery"), [Meenachil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenachil,_Kottayam "Meenachil, Kottayam"), [Poonjar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poonjar "Poonjar") and [Ambalappuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambalappuzha "Ambalappuzha").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-49) In 1729, [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma") founded the princely state of [Thiruvithamkoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") and Thiruvananthapuram was made the capital in 1795 after shifting the capital from [Padmanabhapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmanabhapuram "Padmanabhapuram") in [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari") district.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-district_history-50) Thiruvananthapuram became a prominent city in Kerala under [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Online._Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica_Inc_2013-51)

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/A_language_map_of_India_prepared_for_the_missionary_projects_at_Serampore%2C_1822.jpg/250px-A_language_map_of_India_prepared_for_the_missionary_projects_at_Serampore%2C_1822.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_language_map_of_India_prepared_for_the_missionary_projects_at_Serampore,_1822.jpg)

A language map of India prepared in 1822.

As a result of the annexation of neighbouring [chiefdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiefdom "Chiefdom"), the artists and scholars from these places migrated to Thiruvananthapuram, turning it into a cultural center. [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma") gave patronage to different temple art forms including _Koothu_, _Padhakam_, _[Kathakali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathakali "Kathakali")_, _Thullal_, and _[Koodiyattam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koodiyattam "Koodiyattam")_. Noted artists such as [Ramapurathu Warrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramapurathu_Warrier "Ramapurathu Warrier") and [Kunchan Nambiar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunchan_Nambiar "Kunchan Nambiar") amongst others served as his court poets.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Gauri_Lakshmi_Bayi_1998_152%E2%80%93168-52) Travancore became the most dominant state in Kerala by defeating the powerful [Zamorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamorin "Zamorin") of [Kozhikode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Kozhikode "History of Kozhikode") in the battle of [Purakkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purakkad "Purakkad") in 1755.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-AHoT_162-21)

The city developed into a significant intellectual and artistic centre during this period. The city's golden age was during the mid-19th century under the reign of [Maharaja Swathi Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swathi_Thirunal_Rama_Varma "Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma") and [Maharaja Ayilyam Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayilyam_Thirunal "Ayilyam Thirunal"). This era saw the establishment of the first English school (1834), the [Observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum_Observatory "Trivandrum Observatory") (1837), the General Hospital (1839), [the Oriental Research Institute & Manuscripts Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Oriental_Research_Institute_&_Manuscripts_Library "The Oriental Research Institute & Manuscripts Library") and the University College (1873). The first mental hospital in the state was started during the same period. [Sanskrit College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit_College "Sanskrit College"), [Ayurveda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayurveda "Ayurveda") College, [Law College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_College "Law College") and a second-grade college for women were started by [Moolam Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moolam_Thirunal "Moolam Thirunal") (1885–1924).[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-History_of_Thiruvananthapuram-53)

### Contemporary Period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Contemporary Period")]

The early 20th century was an age of tremendous political and social changes in the city. The [Sree Moolam Popular Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Moolam_Popular_Assembly "Sree Moolam Popular Assembly"), established in 1904, was the first democratically elected legislative council in any Indian state.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-54) Despite not being under the direct control of the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") at any time, the city featured prominently in [India's freedom struggle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"). The [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") had a very active presence in Thiruvananthapuram. A meeting of the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") presided by Dr [Pattabhi Sitaramaiah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattabhi_Sitaramaiah "Pattabhi Sitaramaiah") was held here in 1938. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Palace_of_Trivandrum.jpg/250px-Palace_of_Trivandrum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Palace_of_Trivandrum.jpg)

[Kowdiar Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kowdiar_Palace "Kowdiar Palace") built-in 1915 was the official residence of the [Travancore Royal Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore_Royal_Family "Travancore Royal Family").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Kowdiar-55)

The Thiruvananthapuram Municipality came into existence in 1920 as the first municipality in the [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") region. The municipality was converted into a corporation on 30 October 1940, during the period of [Chitra Thirunal Bala Rama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitra_Thirunal_Bala_Rama_Varma "Chitra Thirunal Bala Rama Varma"), who took over in 1931.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-ThiruvananthapuramHistoryIntro-56) The city witnessed multi-faceted progress during his period. The promulgation of the "[Temple Entry Proclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_Entry_Proclamation "Temple Entry Proclamation")" (1936) was an act that underlined social emancipation. This era also saw the establishment of the [University of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_University "Kerala University") in 1937, which later became [Kerala University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_University "Kerala University").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-University_of_Kerala_History-57)

### Modern Period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Modern Period")]

With the end of British rule in 1947, Travancore chose to join the Indian union. The first popularly elected ministry, headed by [Pattom Thanu Pillai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattom_Thanu_Pillai "Pattom Thanu Pillai"), was installed in office on 24 March 1948. In 1949, Thiruvananthapuram became the capital of [Thiru-Kochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore-Cochin "Travancore-Cochin"), the state formed by the integration of Travancore with its northern neighbour, the [Kochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-58) The king of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"), [Chitra Thirunal Bala Rama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitra_Thirunal_Bala_Rama_Varma "Chitra Thirunal Bala Rama Varma"), became the [Rajpramukh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajpramukh "Rajpramukh") of the [Travancore-Cochin Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore-Cochin "Travancore-Cochin") from 1 July 1949 until 31 October 1956. When the state of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") was formed on 1 November 1956, Thiruvananthapuram became its capital.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-59)

With the establishment of [Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thumba_Equatorial_Rocket_Launching_Station "Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station") (TERLS) in 1962, Thiruvananthapuram became the cradle of India's ambitious space programme. The first Indian space rocket was developed and launched from the [Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikram_Sarabhai_Space_Centre "Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre") (VSSC) in the outskirts of the city in 1963. Several establishments of the [Indian Space Research Organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Space_Research_Organisation "Indian Space Research Organisation") (ISRO) were later established in Thiruvananthapuram.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-VSSC_Thiruvananthapuram-60)

A significant milestone in the city's recent history was the establishment of [Technopark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technopark_Kerala "Technopark Kerala")—India's first IT park—in 1995.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Technopark_Thiruvananthapuram-61) Technopark has developed into the largest IT park in the geographical area,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-62) employing around 62,000 people in 450 companies.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-63)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Geography")]

View of [Pattom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattom "Pattom"), the north eastern part of the city. The [Western Ghats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Ghats "Western Ghats") mountain range is seen in the background

Thiruvananthapuram is built on seven hills[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-64) by the seashore and is at [8°30′N 76°54′E / 8.5°N 76.9°E / 8.5; 76.9](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Thiruvananthapuram&params=8.5_N_76.9_E_) on the west coast, near the southern tip of mainland India.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-65) The city is on the west coast of India and is bounded by the [Laccadive Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laccadive_Sea "Laccadive Sea") to its west and the [Western Ghats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Ghats "Western Ghats") to its east. The average elevation of the city is 16 ft (4.9 m) above [sea level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level "Sea level").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-66) The [Geological Survey of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geological_Survey_of_India "Geological Survey of India") has identified Thiruvananthapuram as a moderately earthquake-prone urban centre and categorised the metropolis in the Seismic III Zone.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-67) Thiruvananthapuram lies on the shores of [Karamana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karamana "Karamana") and [Killi rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killi_river "Killi river"). [Vellayani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vellayani_Lake "Vellayani Lake"), [Thiruvalla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvalla "Thiruvalla") and [Aakulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aakkulam "Aakkulam") backwaters lie in the city.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-68) The soil type in the middle part of the city is a dark brown loamy [laterite soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laterite "Laterite") high in phosphates. Laterisation is a result of the heavy rainfall and humid conditions. In western coastal regions of the city, [sandy loam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loam "Loam") soil is found, and on hilly eastern parts of the district, rich dark brown loam of granite origin is found.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-69)

The [Thiruvananthapuram Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Corporation") is spread over 214.86 km 2 (82.96 sq mi).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-citygi-2) The wider [Thiruvananthapuram metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_metropolitan_area "Thiruvananthapuram metropolitan area") comprises Thiruvananthapuram corporation, three municipalities and 27 panchayats, as of 2011.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-ListofUA-70) Being the largest city in India's southern tip region, it is essential for both military logistics and civil aviation in the southern part of the country. Thiruvananthapuram is the headquarters of the [Southern Air Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Air_Command_(India) "Southern Air Command (India)") (SAC) of the [Indian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Air_Force "Indian Air Force").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Air_Command-71)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Climate")]

The city has a climate that lies on the border between a [tropical savanna climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_savanna_climate "Tropical savanna climate") ([Köppen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")_Aw_) and a [tropical monsoon climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_monsoon_climate "Tropical monsoon climate") (_Am_). As a result, its only distinct seasons relate to rainfall rather than temperature. Temperatures in Thiruvananthapuram remain remarkably stable throughout the year, with an annual mean maximum of about 31–32°C (88–90°F) and a mean minimum around 23–24°C (73–75°F). Daytime highs generally stay between 30 and 34°C (86–93°F), while nights are warm and humid, averaging approximately 22–25°C (72–77°F). The temperature rarely falls below something like both 20°C (68°F) and above 35°C (95°F). The humidity is high and rises to about 90% during the [monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon "Monsoon") season.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Thiruvananthapuram_Weather-72) Thiruvananthapuram is the first city along the path of the [south-west monsoons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South-west_monsoon "South-west monsoon") and gets its first showers in early June. The city receives heavy rainfall of around 1,835 mm (72.2 in) per year. The city also gets rain from the receding north-east monsoons which hit the city by October. The dry season sets in by December. The lowest temperature recorded in the city core was 10.8°C (51.4°F) on 6 January 1974 and it also recorded 15.6°C in Jan 18 in 2015. The highest temperature was 38.2°C (100.8°F) on 21 February 2019.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-IMDextremes-73) At the airport, the lowest temperature recorded was 12.1°C (53.8°F) on 15 January 1975 and the highest temperature was 36.3°C (97.3°F) on 5 May 1998.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-IMDextremes-73)

According to provisional results of the 2011 national census, the Corporation of Thiruvananthapuram, which occupies an area of 214 km 2 (83 sq mi), had a population of 957,730.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-citygi-2) The city's population density was 4,454/km 2 (11,540/sq mi).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-citygi-2) The Urban Agglomeration had a population of 1,687,406 in 2011.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-UApop-4) The sex ratio is 1,040 females for every 1,000 males, which is higher than the national average.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-citygi-2) Thiruvananthapuram's literacy rate of 93.72%[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Citycenpop-81) exceeds the all-India average of 74%.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-censusindliter-82)

It is a historical city where [Malayali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalis "Malayalis") form the vast majority of Thiruvananthapuram's population. There are also minorities like the [Tamils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_people "Tamil people") and North Indians residing here. According to the 2011 census, 68.5% of the population is [Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism "Hinduism"), 16.7% [Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") and 13.7% [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam "Islam").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-CityCensus-83) The remainder of the community includes [Jains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jainism "Jainism"), [Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews "Jews"), [Sikhs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh"), [Buddhists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhist "Buddhist") and other religions which account for 0.06% of the population; 0.85% did not state a belief in the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-CityCensus-83)

[Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam"), the official state language, is the dominant language in Thiruvananthapuram City:[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-84) English is also used, mainly by the [white-collar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-collar_worker "White-collar worker") workforce. [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") has the most speakers after [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam"). The city also has a few [Tulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulu_language "Tulu language"), [Kannada, Konkani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konkani_language "Konkani language"), [Dhivehi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maldivian_language "Maldivian language"), [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") and Hindi speakers. As per the 2001 census, the population below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Below_Poverty_Line_(India) "Below Poverty Line (India)") in the city was 11,667.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Urban_poor_in_Thiruvananthapuram-85)

Thiruvananthapuram has witnessed massive immigration of workers from northern India, mainly [Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab,_India "Punjab, India"), [Haryana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryana "Haryana"), and [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"), and Eastern India, mainly [West Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bengal "West Bengal") and [Bihar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bihar "Bihar"), and from neighbouring countries like [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka"), the [Maldives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maldives "Maldives"), [Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal "Nepal") and [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-86)

## Administration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Administration")]

Main articles: [Administration of Trivandrum district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administration_of_Trivandrum_district "Administration of Trivandrum district") and [Thiruvananthapuram Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Corporation")

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly%2C_Thiruvananthapuram.jpg/250px-Kerala_Legislative_Assembly%2C_Thiruvananthapuram.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kerala_Legislative_Assembly,_Thiruvananthapuram.jpg)

[Kerala Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly") Building

The [Corporation of Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Municipal_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation") or TMC oversees and manages the civic infrastructure of the city's 100 wards.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-citad-87) Each ward elects a [councillor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Councillor "Councillor") to the Corporation of Thiruvananthapuram. TMC has the power to act as the local government of the city.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-orgst-88) TMC is headed by the Mayor, who is elected from among the [councillors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Councillor "Councillor"). The Mayor is responsible for the overall supervision and control of the administrative functions of the TMC. The corporation discharges its services through standing committees.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-orgst-88) The corporation secretary is an officer appointed by the [government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Kerala "Government of Kerala"), who serves as the administrative head of the TMC and implements the council's decisions based on the resolutions adopted by the council. The functions of the Municipal Corporation are managed by seven departments—engineering, health, general administration, council, accounts and revenue.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-orgstruc-89) For the decentralised role of TMC, eleven Zonal Offices are created. The zonal offices are in Fort, Kadakampally, [Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom "Nemom"), [Ulloor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulloor "Ulloor"), Attipra, Thiruvallom, [Kazhakkuttom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakkuttom "Kazhakkuttom"), [Sreekaryam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sreekaryam "Sreekaryam"), [Kudappanakunnu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kudappanakunnu "Kudappanakunnu"), [Vattiyoorkavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattiyoorkavu "Vattiyoorkavu") and [Vizhinjam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vizhinjam "Vizhinjam").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-90) The functions of the TMC include water supply, drainage and sewerage, sanitation, solid-waste management, and building regulation. The [Thiruvananthapuram Development Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Development_Authority "Thiruvananthapuram Development Authority") is responsible for the statutory planning and development of the [greater Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_metropolitan_area "Thiruvananthapuram metropolitan area") region.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-91)

As the seat of the [Government of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Kerala "Government of Kerala"), Thiruvananthapuram is home to not only the offices of the local governing agencies but also the [Kerala Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly") and the state secretariat, which is housed in the [Kerala Government Secretariat complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Government_Secretariat "Kerala Government Secretariat"). Thiruvananthapuram has two parliamentary constituencies—[Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Attingal (Lok Sabha constituency)") and [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Thiruvananthapuram (Lok Sabha constituency)")—and elects five Members of the Legislative Assembly ([MLAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_Legislative_Assembly "Member of the Legislative Assembly")) to the state legislature.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-92)

### Law and order

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Law and order")]

The [Thiruvananthapuram City Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_City_Police "Thiruvananthapuram City Police") is the main law-enforcement agency in the city. It is headed by a [commissioner of police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_commissioner "Police commissioner").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-poli-94) The [Thiruvananthapuram city police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_city_police "Thiruvananthapuram city police") is a division of the [Kerala Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Police "Kerala Police"), and the administrative control lies with the [Kerala Home Ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Home_(Kerala) "Department of Home (Kerala)"). Thiruvananthapuram city police is the largest police division in Kerala, and it consists of four subdivisional offices and 24 police stations and a sanctioned strength of 3,500 police personnel.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-kerpol-95) The [Central Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Prison,_Poojappura "Central Prison, Poojappura") is the oldest prison in Kerala and the headquarters of [Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Prisons_and_Correctional_Services "Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-96)

### Military and diplomatic establishments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Military and diplomatic establishments")]

The [Southern Air Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Air_Command_(India) "Southern Air Command (India)") of the [Indian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Air_Force "Indian Air Force") is headquartered in the city.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-SAC-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-98) There are two state armed police battalions and a unit of the [Central Reserve Police Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Reserve_Police_Force "Central Reserve Police Force") (CRPF) based in Thiruvananthapuram.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-99) The CRPF has a Group Headquarters (GHQ) located at [Pallipuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallippuram,_Thiruvananthapuram "Pallippuram, Thiruvananthapuram").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-100) In addition to this, three units of the [Central Industrial Security Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Industrial_Security_Force "Central Industrial Security Force") (CISF) and Sector Headquarters (SHQ) of the [Border Security Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_Security_Force "Border Security Force") (BSF) are also present. Thiruvananthapuram also houses a large army cantonment in [Pangode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangode "Pangode") which houses some regiments of the [Indian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Army "Indian Army").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-101)

In the city there is a Consulate of the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"),[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-102) a Consulate of the [Maldives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maldives "Maldives"),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-103) and Honorary Consulates of [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka"), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") and [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-105)

### Utility services

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Utility services")]

The [Kerala Water Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Water_Authority "Kerala Water Authority") supplies the city with water that is sourced from the [Karamana River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karamana_River "Karamana River");[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-water-106) most of it is drawn from the [Aruvikkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aruvikkara "Aruvikkara") and [Peppara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peppara_Wildlife_Sanctuary "Peppara Wildlife Sanctuary") reservoirs, and it is treated and purified at the Aruvikkara pumping stations.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-107) The Wellington Water Works, commissioned in 1933, is one of the oldest city water supply schemes in India.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-108) The sewage water is treated at Muttathara sewage-treatment plant, which handles 32 million litres per day.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-110) The city area is divided into seven blocks for the execution of the sewage system.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-111) Electricity is supplied by the [Kerala State Electricity Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Electricity_Board "Kerala State Electricity Board").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-112) Fire services are handled by the [Kerala Fire And Rescue Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Fire_And_Rescue_Services "Kerala Fire And Rescue Services").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-113)

Thiruvananthapuram is strategically located just 10 nautical miles (19 km; 12 mi) away from the crucial [Suez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suez "Suez") to [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore") Far East international shipping route, placing it in close proximity to key global maritime traffic. This advantageous location, combined with the availability of reliable electricity, fresh water, and a long coastline, has accelerated industrial growth in the city. Thiruvananthapuram's economy comprises [Information Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_Technology "Information Technology"), education, plantations, aerospace, commerce and [tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism "Tourism").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-sceco-114) Thiruvananthapuram district contributes 10.31%, of the state's GDP.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-ecrev-115) With an economic growth rate of 13.83%, Thiruvananthapuram is the fastest-growing district in Kerala.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-ecrev-115) Thiruvananthapuram was listed as one of the top ten cities in India on Vibrancy and Consumption Index by a study conducted by global [financial services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_services "Financial services") firm [Morgan Stanley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Stanley "Morgan Stanley").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-MorStan-116) State- and central-government employees make up a large percentage of the city's workforce.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-ecrev-115)

**Thiruvananthapuram** (Malayalam pronunciation:[[t̪iɾuʋənən̪d̪ɐˈbuɾəm]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/b/b9/Trivandrum.ogg/Trivandrum.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Trivandrum.ogg "File:Trivandrum.ogg")[_tirr-ROO-və-nun-Tə-poor-əm_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")), also known as **Trivandrum**, is the [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_city "Capital city") city of the Indian state of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-10) As of 2011, the [Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Municipal_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation") had a population of 957,730 over an area of 214.86 km 2,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-citypop-11) making it the most populous city in Kerala.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-districtprofile-12) The larger [Thiruvananthapuram metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_metropolitan_area "Thiruvananthapuram metropolitan area") has over 1.7 million inhabitants within an area of 543 km 2, making it the second-most populous [metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area") in Kerala after [Kochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi_metropolitan_area "Kochi metropolitan area").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-uapop-13) Thiruvananthapuram is one of the few cities in India that serves as a state capital and is also centre for heritage, maritime activities, information technology, research and development, space research, defence, automotive technology, and biosciences. It is also among the few cities in the world where both an [international airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum_International_Airport "Trivandrum International Airport") and an [international seaport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vizhinjam_International_Seaport_Thiruvananthapuram "Vizhinjam International Seaport Thiruvananthapuram") are located within the city in close proximity to the city center.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-14)

Located on the west coast of India near the extreme south of the mainland, Thiruvananthapuram is a port city located 10 [nautical miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile "Nautical mile") (19 km; 12 mi)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-15) from a heavily trafficked east–west shipping channel. The city is home to India's first deep-water trans-shipment port, the [Vizhinjam International Seaport Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vizhinjam_International_Seaport_Thiruvananthapuram "Vizhinjam International Seaport Thiruvananthapuram").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-16) The city is characterised by its undulating terrain of low coastal hills.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-17) Thiruvananthapuram is also known for its cultural heritage, being associated with the musical contributions of [Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swathi_Thirunal "Swathi Thirunal") and the artistic legacy of painter Raja Ravi Varma. Thiruvananthapuram has contributed to the development of [Malayalam literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_literature "Malayalam literature") through individuals like [Ulloor S. Parameswara Iyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulloor_S._Parameswara_Iyer "Ulloor S. Parameswara Iyer"), [Kumaran Asan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumaran_Asan "Kumaran Asan"), [C. V. Raman Pillai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._V._Raman_Pillai "C. V. Raman Pillai") and [Narayana Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narayana_Guru "Narayana Guru"). The city is also known for [Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Padmanabhaswamy_Temple "Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple"), known as the richest temple in the world.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-18) The other temples includes the Sreevaraham temple, the Shreekanteswaram temple and the Attukal Bhagavathy temple.

The present regions that constitute Thiruvananthapuram were ruled by the [Ays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_kingdom "Ay kingdom") who were related to feudatories of the [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19) In the 12th century, it was conquered by the [Kingdom of Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19) In the 18th century, the king [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_varma "Marthanda varma") expanded the territory, founded the princely state of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") and made Thiruvananthapuram its capital.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-history1-20)[Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") became the most dominant state in Kerala by defeating the powerful [Zamorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamorin "Zamorin") of [Calicut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Calicut "History of Calicut") in the battle of [Purakkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purakkad "Purakkad") in 1755.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-AHoT_162-21) Following [India's independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement") in 1947, Thiruvananthapuram became the capital of [Travancore–Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore%E2%80%93Cochin "Travancore–Cochin") state and remained so until the new Indian state of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") was formed in 1956.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-23)

Thiruvananthapuram is a notable academic and research hub and home to the [University of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kerala "University of Kerala"), [APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APJ_Abdul_Kalam_Technological_University "APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University"), the regional headquarters of [Indira Gandhi National Open University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi_National_Open_University "Indira Gandhi National Open University"), and many other schools and colleges. Thiruvananthapuram is also home to research centres such as the [National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_for_Interdisciplinary_Science_and_Technology "National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology"), [Indian Space Research Organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Space_Research_Organisation "Indian Space Research Organisation")'s [Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikram_Sarabhai_Space_Centre "Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre"), the [Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Space_Science_and_Technology "Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology"), [National Centre for Earth Science Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Centre_for_Earth_Science_Studies "National Centre for Earth Science Studies") and a campus of the [Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institutes_of_Science_Education_and_Research "Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-24) Thiruvananthapuram is where India's space program began, with the headquarters of [Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Propulsion_Systems_Centre "Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre") located there. The city is home to media institutions like [Toonz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toonz "Toonz") Animation India and [Tata Elxsi Ltd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tata_Elxsi "Tata Elxsi"), and also to [Chitranjali Film Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitranjali_Studio "Chitranjali Studio"), one of the first film studios in [Malayalam Cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_Cinema "Malayalam Cinema"), and [Kinfra Film and Video Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinfra_Film_and_Video_Park "Kinfra Film and Video Park") at [Kazhakoottam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakoottam "Kazhakoottam"), which is India's first infotainment industrial park.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-25)

In 2012, Thiruvananthapuram was named the best Kerala city to live in, by a field survey conducted by _[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-26) In 2013, the city was ranked the fifteenth best city to live in India, in a survey conducted by _[India Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India\_Today "India Today")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-India_Today_survey-27) Thiruvananthapuram was ranked the best Indian city for two consecutive years, 2015 and 2016, according to the Annual Survey of India's City-Systems (ASICS) conducted by the [Janaagraha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janaagraha "Janaagraha") Centre for Citizenship and Democracy.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Best_Indian_City-28) The city was also selected as the best governed city in India in a survey conducted by Janaagraha Centre for citizenship and democracy in 2017.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Best_Governed_City-29)

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

The city takes its name from the [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam") word _thiru-anantha-puram_ (തിരുവനന്തപുരം[[t̪iɾuʋɐnɐn̪d̪ɐpuɾɐm]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/8/86/En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga/En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga "File:En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga")), meaning "The City of Lord Anantha (means infinite, endless, or eternal)",[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Meaning_of_name-30) referring to the [deity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deity "Deity") of the [Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Padmanabhaswamy_Temple "Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple") located in the city. Thiruvananthapuram is also known in literature, and popular reference as _Ananthapuri_, derived from the [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") word _Syanandurapuram_, meaning "The City of Bliss" in Carnatic [kirtanas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirtan "Kirtan") composed by [Swathi Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swathi_Thirunal "Swathi Thirunal"), erstwhile Maharaja of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-31) The city was officially referred to as _Trivandrum_ until 1991 (Trivandrum being the anglicised name of the town), when the government decided to reinstate the city's original name Thiruvananthapuram. Many Malayalees still refer to the city as Trivandrum, however.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-32) The city was also called as _Anandapatnam_ or _Anandapatam_ in [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") and [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") languages meaning "The City of Ananda" which is the same to meaning for the original name. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Pre Historic Period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Pre Historic Period")]

Thiruvananthapuram is a relatively modern region with trading traditions dating back to 1000 BCE.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-34) It is believed that the ships of [King Solomon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon "Solomon") landed in a port then called [Ophir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ophir "Ophir") (now [Poovar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poovar "Poovar")) in Thiruvananthapuram in 1036 BCE.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-36) The city was the trading post of [spices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spices "Spices"), [sandalwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandalwood "Sandalwood") and [ivory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivory "Ivory").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-Ancient_Trade_in_Thiruvananthapuram-37) However, the ancient political and cultural history of the city was almost entirely independent from that of the rest of Kerala. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Ancient Period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Ancient Period")]

The southern region of present-day Kerala state (The coastal belt between Thiruvananthapuram and [Alappuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alappuzha "Alappuzha")) was under [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty"), which was more related to the [Pandya dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty") of [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai "Madurai").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-38)[_[page needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_] The early rulers of the city were the [Ays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_kingdom "Ay kingdom"). [Vizhinjam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vizhinjam "Vizhinjam"), which is now a region in the present-day Thiruvananthapuram, was the capital of the [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-39) Vizhinjam was an important port city from as early as the second century BC.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-41) During the Ay dynasty's rule, Thiruvananthapuram witnessed many battles in which the [Chola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty") and [Pandyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandyan_dynasty "Pandyan dynasty") dynasties attempted to capture the port town.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis1-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis2-43)

### Middle Ages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Middle Ages")]

After the death of king [Vikramaditya Varaguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikramaditya_Varaguna "Vikramaditya Varaguna") in 925 AD, the glory of the Ays departed and almost all their territories became part of the [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-44)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19) During the tenth century, the Cholas attacked and sacked Vizhinjam and surrounding regions.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19) The port in Vizhinjam and the historic education center of Kanthalloor Sala were also destroyed by Cholas during this period.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-kanthalloor-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-46) A branch of the Ay family, which had controlled the [Padmanabhaswamy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmanabhaswamy_Temple "Padmanabhaswamy Temple"), merged with the [Kingdom of Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad") in the 12th century.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram#cite_note-vizhis3-19)
