"List of districts of Kerala") in the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India "States and union territories of India") of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). The district was created in 1949, with its headquarters in the city of Thiruvananthapuram, which is also Kerala's administrative centre. The present district was created in 1956 by separating the four southernmost Taluks of the erstwhile district to form [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"). The city of Thiruvananthapuram is also known as the [Information technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology "Information technology") capital of the state, since it is home to the first and largest IT park in India, [Technopark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technopark,_Trivandrum "Technopark, Trivandrum"), established in 1990. The district is home to more than 9% of total population of the state.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-8) The district covers an area of 2,192 square kilometres (541,655 acres). At the 2011 census, it had a population of 3,301,427,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-District_population-10) making it the second most populous district in Kerala after [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-districtcensus-11) Its population density is the highest in Kerala, with 1,509 inhabitants per square kilometre (3,910/sq mi).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-Kerala_Provisional_Population_Totals-12) The district is divided into six [subdistricts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil"): [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_taluk "Thiruvananthapuram taluk"), [Chirayinkeezhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirayinkeezhu_taluk "Chirayinkeezhu taluk"), [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara_taluk "Neyyattinkara taluk"), [Nedumangadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedumangad_taluk "Nedumangad taluk"), [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala"), and [Kattakada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattakada "Kattakada"). The urban bodies in the district are the [Thiruvananthapuram Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Municipal_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation"), and the [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala"), [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara "Neyyattinkara"), [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal"), and [Nedumangad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedumangad "Nedumangad") municipalities.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-13) Thiruvananthapuram district is located between ![Image 18: Show location on an interactive map](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/WMA_button2b.png/20px-WMA_button2b.png)WikiMiniAtlas [8°10′N 76°25′E / 8.17°N 76.41°E / 8.17; 76.41](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Thiruvananthapuram_district¶ms=8.17_N_76.41_E_) and ![Image 19: Show location on an interactive map](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/WMA_button2b.png/20px-WMA_button2b.png)WikiMiniAtlas [8°32′N 77°10′E / 8.54°N 77.17°E / 8.54; 77.17](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Thiruvananthapuram_district¶ms=8.54_N_77.17_E_). At the southernmost extremity of the district, Kaliyikkavila is 54 kilometres (34 mi) from [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari"), the southernmost point on the Indian peninsula.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-14) 33.75% of the district population lives in urban areas.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-15) The district has three major rivers, several freshwater lakes, and over 300 ponds. Its eastern region is forested, northern regions are mostly under rubber cultivation and the remaining areas grow mixed dry-land crops of coconut, plantain, and tapioca, among others. Built-up areas and rice fields complete the land use pattern.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-16) ## Etymology [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Etymology")] The name Thiruvananthapuram, shared by the district and its headquarters city, comes from the [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam")/[Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") word "Thiru" and [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit_language "Sanskrit language") word "anantha-pura", meaning "Abode of Lord Anantha".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-Meaning_of_name-17) The name derives from the deity of the [Hindu temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_temple "Hindu temple") at the center of Thiruvananthapuram city. Anantha is another name of Vishnu, the deity of [Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Padmanabhaswamy_temple "Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple"). The district's official name in English was Trivandrum until 1991, when the government reinstated the city's original name, Thiruvananthapuram, in all languages. ## History [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: History")] See also: [Merger of Kanyakumari with Madras State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merger_of_Kanyakumari_with_Madras_State "Merger of Kanyakumari with Madras State") [![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Kanakakkunnu_Palace_DSW.jpg/250px-Kanakakkunnu_Palace_DSW.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kanakakkunnu_Palace_DSW.jpg) [Kanakakkunnu Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanakakkunnu_Palace "Kanakakkunnu Palace") at Thiruvananthapuram The city of Thiruvananthapuram features several landmarks with regards to ancient tradition, folklore, and literature. Several other locations in the district feature similar landmarks. The [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty") governed the area of [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") between [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari") in the south to [Kasaragod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasaragod "Kasaragod") in the north. This included [Palakkad Gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palakkad_Gap "Palakkad Gap"), [Coimbatore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coimbatore "Coimbatore"), [Salem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salem,_Tamil_Nadu "Salem, Tamil Nadu"), and [Kolli Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolli_Hills "Kolli Hills"). The region around [Coimbatore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coimbatore "Coimbatore") served as the eastern entrance to the [Palakkad Gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palakkad_Gap "Palakkad Gap"), the mountain pass that is the principal trade route between the [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") and [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-Trade-18) The southernmost region of present-day Malabar coast (the coastal belt between Kanyakumari and Kollam) was ruled by the [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty"), who were related to, and officially feudatories of the Cheras.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-19) The Ay Dynasty (later known as the Venad Dynasty and finally the Thiruvithamkur Dynasty), followed by the Nannan Dynasty (later known as the [Mushika dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushika_dynasty "Mushika dynasty") and finally the [Kolathiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolathiri "Kolathiri") dynasty), were the two oldest and most important lineages of the [Velir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velir "Velir") clan, who had very frequent intermarriages with the Cheras, [Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty"), and the [Pandyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-24) Present-day Thiruvananthapuram city, district, and [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"), were ruled by the [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty") during ancient and medieval ages, which was a [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") kingdom based in the southernmost part of Indian Subcontinent.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) Ay kingdom had experienced attacks and conquests by [Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty") and [Pandyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty") in various periods.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) Later it became a part of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad") in late Middle Ages, which was eventually expanded as the powerful kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") in 18th century CE.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) The [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamils "Tamils")-Dravidian kind of architecture is also found in Padmanabhaswamy temple, which makes it distinct from the architectural style of temples in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") in general.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) [![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/1733_Homann_Heirs_Map_of_India_-_Geographicus_-_India-homannheirs-1733.jpg/250px-1733_Homann_Heirs_Map_of_India_-_Geographicus_-_India-homannheirs-1733.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1733_Homann_Heirs_Map_of_India_-_Geographicus_-_India-homannheirs-1733.jpg) A map of [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") drawn by Homann Heirs in 1733. At that time, Travancore was only a small territory wedged between [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam") and [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari"), as shown in the map (Present-day districts of Trivandrum and Kanyakumari only).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-:302-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-:3-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-majumdar407-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-:6-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-31) In 1684, during the [regency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regent "Regent") of [Umayamma Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umayamma_Rani "Umayamma Rani"), the [English East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_East_India_Company "English East India Company") acquired a sandy spit of land at [Anchuthengu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchuthengu "Anchuthengu"), near [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala") on the sea coast about 32 kilometres (20 mi) north of Thiruvananthapuram city, with a view to erecting a factory and fortifying it. The location had earlier been frequented by the Dutch, then by the British. It was from here that the English gradually extended their diplomacy to other parts of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-32) [![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Travancore_1871.JPG/250px-Travancore_1871.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Travancore_1871.JPG) A map of the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj")[Princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") published in 1871 Modern history begins with [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma") (1729 CE–1758 CE), generally regarded as the Father of modern [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). In the early 18th century CE, the [Travancore royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore_royal_family "Travancore royal family") adopted some members from the royal family of [Kolathunadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolathunadu "Kolathunadu") (a long separated younger sister dynasty of Ay/Venad/Thiruvithamkur with whom they had the tradition of mutual adoption of heirs for centuries) based in [Kannur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannur "Kannur").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-33) Thiruvananthapuram was known as a great center of intellectual and artistic activity at this time. [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") became the most dominant state in Kerala by defeating the powerful [Zamorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamorin "Zamorin") of [Kozhikode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Kozhikode "History of Kozhikode") in the battle of [Purakkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purakkad "Purakkad") in 1755.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-AHoT_162-34) The temple of Vishnu reclining on Anantha, the [Sri Padmanabhaswamy temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Padmanabhaswamy_temple "Sri Padmanabhaswamy temple"), is the most recognizable and iconic landmark of the city and the district and dates back to the times of the Azhvars, and is one among the 108 shrines mentioned in their texts. In addition to the presiding deity of [Padmanabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishnu "Vishnu"), this temple contains several shrines, dedicated to [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna "Krishna"), [Narasimha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narasimha "Narasimha") and [Ayyappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayyappa "Ayyappa"). King Marthanda Varma, after his conquest of Southern Kerala upto the Aluva, submitted the kingdom to Padmanabha and took upon the title of 'Sree Padmanabhadasa', the Servant of Sree Padmanabha. The vast temple complex, with its tall [Gopuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopuram "Gopuram") decorated with detailed carvings reflected in a huge [temple tank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_tank "Temple tank"), is today a center of attraction for devotees and sightseers. The city was the capital of the [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") state from 18th century CE until [India's independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"). The Thiruvananthapuram Municipality came into existence in 1920 as the first municipality in [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") region. After two decades, during the reign of [Sree Chithira Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Chithira_Thirunal "Sree Chithira Thirunal"), Thiruvananthapuram Municipality was converted into Corporation on 30 October 1940.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-35) Consequent to the recommendations of the State Reorganization Commission, the Vilavancode subdistrict of Thiruvananthapuram was merged with [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu"), along with another three southern subdistricts, Thovala, Agastheewaram, and Kalkulam from [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") which eventually formed Tamil Nadu's [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"). The state of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") came into being on 1 November 1956. ### Kilimanoor palace [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Kilimanoor palace")] See also: [Kilimanoor palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_palace "Kilimanoor palace") [![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Studiorrv.jpg/250px-Studiorrv.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Studiorrv.jpg) Birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma with his studio in the foreground In 1705 ([ME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_era "Malayalam era") 880) the son and two daughters of Ittammar Raja of [Parappanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanad "Parappanad") royal house (originally based at [Parappanangadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanangadi "Parappanangadi") in present-day [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district")) were adopted into the Royal house of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad"). Ittammar Raja's sister and her sons, Rama Varma and Raghava Varma, settled in Kilimanoor and married the now adopted sisters. [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma"), the founder of the Kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"), was the son of Raghava Varma. The nephew[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-36) of Raghava Varma, Ravi Varma Koil Thampuran, married the sister of Marthanda Varma. Their son became known as [Dharma Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharma_Raja "Dharma Raja") Kartika Thirunnal Rama Varma. In 1740 when an allied force,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-37) led by Dutchman Captain Hockert supporting the Deshinganadu King, attacked Venad, an army from Kilimanoor resisted and then defeated them. Although a small victory, this was the first time an Indian army had defeated a European power. In 1753, in recognition of this feat, Marthanda Varma exempted the areas controlled by the Kilimanoor palace[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-38) from taxes, and granted them autonomous status.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-39) The present palace complex was built at this time, together with the Ayyappa temple.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-40) for the family deity, _Sastha_ or Ayyapan.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] [Velu Thampi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velu_Thampi_Dalawa "Velu Thampi Dalawa")[Dalawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewan "Dewan") held meetings at Kilimanoor palace while planning uprisings against the British. He handed over his sword at the palace before going into his final battle against the British, and India's first President, Dr [Rajendra Prasad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajendra_Prasad "Rajendra Prasad") received this sword from the palace and it was kept in the [National Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum,_New_Delhi "National Museum, New Delhi") in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"). Afterwards the sword was moved to the Napier Museum, Thiruvananthapuram. ## Geography [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Geography")] Main article: [Geography of Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Thiruvananthapuram "Geography of Thiruvananthapuram") [![Image 24: A panoramic view of Varkala Beach Cliff](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/37/Panoramic_view_of_varkala_beach_cliff.jpg/1280px-Panoramic_view_of_varkala_beach_cliff.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Panoramic_view_of_varkala_beach_cliff.jpg "A panoramic view of Varkala Beach Cliff") [](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Panoramic_view_of_varkala_beach_cliff.jpg "File:Panoramic view of varkala beach cliff.jpg") A panoramic view of [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala") Beach [Cliff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliff "Cliff") The district is located between ![Image 25: Show location on an interactive map](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/WMA_button2b.png/20px-WMA_button2b.png)WikiMiniAtlas [8°10′N 76°25′E / 8.17°N 76.41°E / 8.17; 76.41](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Thiruvananthapuram_district¶ms=8.17_N_76.41_E_) and ![Image 26: Show location on an interactive map](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/WMA_button2b.png/20px-WMA_button2b.png)WikiMiniAtlas [8°32′N 77°10′E / 8.54°N 77.17°E / 8.54; 77.17](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Thiruvananthapuram_district¶ms=8.54_N_77.17_E_). The southernmost part of the city, [Parassala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parassala "Parassala"), is just 54 kilometres (34 mi) away from the southern [peninsular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peninsular "Peninsular") tip of India, [Cape Comorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_(town) "Kanyakumari (town)") (Kanyakumari). The district stretches 78 kilometres (48 mi) along the shores of the [Arabian Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea") on the west. [Kollam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam_district "Kollam district") lies to the north, with the [Tirunelveli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirunelveli_district "Tirunelveli district") and [Kanyakumari districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district") of [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu") to the east and south respectively.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-41) ### Climate [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Climate")] The climate of Thiruvananthapuram district is generally hot and [tropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropics "Tropics"). Large forest reserves have a favorable effect on the climate and induce rains. Cold weather is experienced in the [mountain ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Ghats "Western Ghats"). Lower down, the weather is bracing, and generally hot in the coastal regions. The mean maximum temperature is 95°F (35°C) and the mean minimum temperature is 69°F (20°C). As the district stretches from north to south, with the [Arabian Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea") to the west, the [relative humidity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relative_humidity "Relative humidity") is generally high. It rises to about 95% during the [southwest monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon#Southwest_monsoon "Monsoon").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-42) The total annual rainfall in the district is about 1,827.7 mm (72 in) per annum.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-43) The southwest monsoon, from June to September is the principal rainy season, during which the district receives most of its annual rainfall. The second rainy season is the [Northeast monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon#Northeast_monsoon "Monsoon"), from October to November. The district also experiences thunderstorm rains in the pre-monsoon months of April and May.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-44) December to February are the coolest months. The average temperature drops to 69°F (20°C) in these months, generally considered India's [winter season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_India#winter "Climate of India"). The [summer season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_India#Summer "Climate of India") starts in February and continues until May. [](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pattom_Skyline_panoramo_02.jpg "File:Pattom Skyline panoramo 02.jpg") A view of the city of Thiruvananthapuram from [Pattom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattom "Pattom"). The media and [information technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology_in_India "Information technology in India") sectors are mainstays of Thiruvananthapuram district's economy, and other major sectors are tourism and [leisure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leisure "Leisure"), agriculture, and education. India's first animation park, the [Kinfra Animation Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinfra_Film_and_Video_Park "Kinfra Film and Video Park"), is in the district. [![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Technopark_Trivandum_Ganga_and_Yamuna_Buildings.jpg/250px-Technopark_Trivandum_Ganga_and_Yamuna_Buildings.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Technopark_Trivandum_Ganga_and_Yamuna_Buildings.jpg) A [Technopark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technopark_Kerala "Technopark Kerala") building. Technopark as of 2010 has 450,000 m 2 (4,800,000 sq ft) of built-up space, and is home to over 200 companies, employing around 30,000 professionals. Thiruvananthapuram district has 2 central-sector, 14 state-sector, 1 co-operative-sector, 4 joint-sector, and 60 private-sector medium- and large-scale enterprises. As of 31 March 2003, [Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Industrial_Development_Corporation "Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation") (KSIDC) units employed 9,262 people, and had invested Rs. 3439.4 million.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-48) In 2002, there were 901 registered working factories, including oil mills, cashew factories, [Cotton mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton_mill "Cotton mill"), [Sawmills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawmill "Sawmill"), [printing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offset_printing "Offset printing"), rubber industrial units, chemical units, match factories, general engineering units, and automobile workshops. The Shree Mulam Thirunal Shashtiabdapoorthy Memorial Institute (S.M.S.M. Institute) in Thiruvananthapuram city is a major state government emporium marketing products of Kerala's [handicraft industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handicraft "Handicraft"). The Neyyar Irrigation Project, commissioned in 1959, irrigates an area of 116.65 km 2 (45.0 sq mi). The [Neyyar river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyar_(river) "Neyyar (river)") is the source of water for the [Neyyar reservoir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyar_Dam "Neyyar Dam"). The dam is 294.13 metres (965.0 ft) long and 50.6 metres (166.0 ft) high. The catchment draining into the reservoir, covering an area of 140 km 2 (54 sq mi) of forest, receives an annual average rainfall of about 2,260 mm (90 in) 2260 mm from the two monsoons. [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit§ion=17 "Edit section: Local governance")] Local governance in Thiruvananthapuram district is administered through a three-tier system under the Kerala Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, along with urban local bodies governed by the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994. The rural areas of the district are managed by [gram panchayats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_panchayat "Gram panchayat") at the village level, [block panchayats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panchayat_samiti "Panchayat samiti") at the intermediate level, and the [district panchayat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_council_(India) "District council (India)") at the apex. Urban areas are governed by [municipal corporations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation_(India) "Municipal corporation (India)") and [municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_council_(India) "Municipal council (India)"). Thiruvananthapuram district has one municipal corporation — the [Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Corporation") — and several municipalities, including [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara "Neyyattinkara"), [Nedumangad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedumangad "Nedumangad"), [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal"), [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala"), and [Kattakada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattakada "Kattakada"). The district panchayat oversees the coordinated development of rural local bodies, while urban bodies function independently under their respective councils.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-52) Local government institutions in Thiruvananthapuram district| Level of local government | Number of entities | | --- | --- | | [District Panchayat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_council_(India) "District council (India)") | 1 | | [Block Panchayats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panchayat_samiti "Panchayat samiti") | 11 | | [Gram Panchayats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_panchayat "Gram panchayat") | 78 | | [Municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_urban_local_bodies_in_Kerala "List of urban local bodies in Kerala") | 4 | | [Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Municipal_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation") | 1 | ## Politics [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit§ion=18 "Edit section: Politics")] Thiruvananthapuram district sees a dynamic political landscape with major alliances led by the [Communist Party of India (Marxist)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India_(Marxist) "Communist Party of India (Marxist)") and the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"). Transport [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit§ion=22 "Edit section: Transport")] Main article: [Transport in Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_in_Thiruvananthapuram "Transport in Thiruvananthapuram") [![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Lulumalltrivandrum.jpg/250px-Lulumalltrivandrum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lulumalltrivandrum.jpg) A highway at [Akkulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akkulam "Akkulam") in Thiruvananthapuram National Highway 66 (formerly known as [National Highway 47](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_47_(India) "National Highway 47 (India)")) stretches from Kaliyikkavila at its southern end to [Navaikulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navaikulam "Navaikulam") near [Parippally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parippally "Parippally") in the north, covering a distance of 80 km (50 mi) within the district.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-58) The [Main Central Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Central_Road "Main Central Road") covers a distance of 55 km (34 mi), passing through [Kesavadasapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kesavadasapuram "Kesavadasapuram"), [Vembayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vembayam "Vembayam"), [Venjaramoodu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venjaramoodu "Venjaramoodu"), [Kilimanoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor "Kilimanoor"), and [Nilamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilamel "Nilamel") in the north. The [Kerala Public Works Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Public_Works_Department "Kerala Public Works Department") maintains some 1,552 km (964 mi) of road in the district. Local bodies are responsible for the maintenance of 9,500 km (5,900 mi) of road. There are 116 bridges in Thiruvananthapuram District. Rail transport in the district is operated by [Southern Railway zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Railway_Zone_(India) "Southern Railway Zone (India)") of [Indian Railways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Railways "Indian Railways"). Thiruvananthapuram is connected to the rest of the country by [broad gauge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broad_gauge "Broad gauge") railway line. 82 km (51 mi) of railway line passes through the district.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-59) Thiruvananthapuram district currently has 20 stations, including [Thiruvananthapuram Central railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Central_railway_station "Thiruvananthapuram Central railway station"). Domestic and international airlines operate from [Thiruvananthapuram International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_International_Airport "Thiruvananthapuram International Airport"), which has direct flights to many international cities, including [Kuwait City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait_City "Kuwait City"), [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai"), [Dammam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dammam "Dammam"), [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore"), [Malé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mal%C3%A9 "Malé"), [Colombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo "Colombo"), [Sharjah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharjah_(city) "Sharjah (city)"), [Muscat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscat,_Oman "Muscat, Oman"), [Manama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manama "Manama"), [Doha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doha "Doha"), [Jeddah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeddah "Jeddah"), and [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi"). **Thiruvananthapuram district** (Malayalam:[[t̪iɾuʋɐnɐn̪d̪ɐpuɾɐm]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/8/86/En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga/En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga "File:En-Thiruvananthapuram.oga")) is the [southernmost district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_districts_of_Kerala "List of districts of Kerala") in the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India "States and union territories of India") of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). The district was created in 1949, with its headquarters in the city of Thiruvananthapuram, which is also Kerala's administrative centre. The present district was created in 1956 by separating the four southernmost Taluks of the erstwhile district to form [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"). The city of Thiruvananthapuram is also known as the [Information technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology "Information technology") capital of the state, since it is home to the first and largest IT park in India, [Technopark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technopark,_Trivandrum "Technopark, Trivandrum"), established in 1990. The district is home to more than 9% of total population of the state.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-8)

The district covers an area of 2,192 square kilometres (541,655 acres). At the 2011 census, it had a population of 3,301,427,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-District_population-10) making it the second most populous district in Kerala after [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-districtcensus-11) Its population density is the highest in Kerala, with 1,509 inhabitants per square kilometre (3,910/sq mi).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-Kerala_Provisional_Population_Totals-12) The district is divided into six [subdistricts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil"): [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_taluk "Thiruvananthapuram taluk"), [Chirayinkeezhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirayinkeezhu_taluk "Chirayinkeezhu taluk"), [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara_taluk "Neyyattinkara taluk"), [Nedumangadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedumangad_taluk "Nedumangad taluk"), [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala"), and [Kattakada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattakada "Kattakada"). The urban bodies in the district are the [Thiruvananthapuram Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Municipal_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation"), and the [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala"), [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara "Neyyattinkara"), [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal"), and [Nedumangad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedumangad "Nedumangad") municipalities.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-13)

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

The name Thiruvananthapuram, shared by the district and its headquarters city, comes from the [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam")/[Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") word "Thiru" and [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit_language "Sanskrit language") word "anantha-pura", meaning "Abode of Lord Anantha".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-Meaning_of_name-17) The name derives from the deity of the [Hindu temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_temple "Hindu temple") at the center of Thiruvananthapuram city. Anantha is another name of Vishnu, the deity of [Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Padmanabhaswamy_temple "Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple"). The district's official name in English was Trivandrum until 1991, when the government reinstated the city's original name, Thiruvananthapuram, in all languages.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

See also: [Merger of Kanyakumari with Madras State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merger_of_Kanyakumari_with_Madras_State "Merger of Kanyakumari with Madras State")

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Kanakakkunnu_Palace_DSW.jpg/250px-Kanakakkunnu_Palace_DSW.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kanakakkunnu_Palace_DSW.jpg)

[Kanakakkunnu Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanakakkunnu_Palace "Kanakakkunnu Palace") at Thiruvananthapuram

The city of Thiruvananthapuram features several landmarks with regards to ancient tradition, folklore, and literature. Several other locations in the district feature similar landmarks. The [Chera dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chera_dynasty "Chera dynasty") governed the area of [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") between [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari") in the south to [Kasaragod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasaragod "Kasaragod") in the north. This included [Palakkad Gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palakkad_Gap "Palakkad Gap"), [Coimbatore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coimbatore "Coimbatore"), [Salem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salem,_Tamil_Nadu "Salem, Tamil Nadu"), and [Kolli Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolli_Hills "Kolli Hills"). The region around [Coimbatore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coimbatore "Coimbatore") served as the eastern entrance to the [Palakkad Gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palakkad_Gap "Palakkad Gap"), the mountain pass that is the principal trade route between the [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") and [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-Trade-18) The southernmost region of present-day Malabar coast (the coastal belt between Kanyakumari and Kollam) was ruled by the [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty"), who were related to, and officially feudatories of the Cheras.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-19) The Ay Dynasty (later known as the Venad Dynasty and finally the Thiruvithamkur Dynasty), followed by the Nannan Dynasty (later known as the [Mushika dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushika_dynasty "Mushika dynasty") and finally the [Kolathiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolathiri "Kolathiri") dynasty), were the two oldest and most important lineages of the [Velir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velir "Velir") clan, who had very frequent intermarriages with the Cheras, [Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty"), and the [Pandyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-24)

Present-day Thiruvananthapuram city, district, and [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"), were ruled by the [Ay dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ay_dynasty "Ay dynasty") during ancient and medieval ages, which was a [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") kingdom based in the southernmost part of Indian Subcontinent.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) Ay kingdom had experienced attacks and conquests by [Cholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chola_dynasty "Chola dynasty") and [Pandyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandya_dynasty "Pandya dynasty") in various periods.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) Later it became a part of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad") in late Middle Ages, which was eventually expanded as the powerful kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") in 18th century CE.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25) The [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamils "Tamils")-Dravidian kind of architecture is also found in Padmanabhaswamy temple, which makes it distinct from the architectural style of temples in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") in general.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-askh-25)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/1733_Homann_Heirs_Map_of_India_-_Geographicus_-_India-homannheirs-1733.jpg/250px-1733_Homann_Heirs_Map_of_India_-_Geographicus_-_India-homannheirs-1733.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1733_Homann_Heirs_Map_of_India_-_Geographicus_-_India-homannheirs-1733.jpg)

A map of [Malabar Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malabar_Coast "Malabar Coast") drawn by Homann Heirs in 1733. At that time, Travancore was only a small territory wedged between [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam") and [Kanyakumari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari "Kanyakumari"), as shown in the map (Present-day districts of Trivandrum and Kanyakumari only).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-:302-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-:3-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-majumdar407-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-:6-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-31)

In 1684, during the [regency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regent "Regent") of [Umayamma Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umayamma_Rani "Umayamma Rani"), the [English East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_East_India_Company "English East India Company") acquired a sandy spit of land at [Anchuthengu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchuthengu "Anchuthengu"), near [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala") on the sea coast about 32 kilometres (20 mi) north of Thiruvananthapuram city, with a view to erecting a factory and fortifying it. The location had earlier been frequented by the Dutch, then by the British. It was from here that the English gradually extended their diplomacy to other parts of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-32)

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Travancore_1871.JPG/250px-Travancore_1871.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Travancore_1871.JPG)

A map of the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj")[Princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") published in 1871

Modern history begins with [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma") (1729 CE–1758 CE), generally regarded as the Father of modern [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). In the early 18th century CE, the [Travancore royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore_royal_family "Travancore royal family") adopted some members from the royal family of [Kolathunadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolathunadu "Kolathunadu") (a long separated younger sister dynasty of Ay/Venad/Thiruvithamkur with whom they had the tradition of mutual adoption of heirs for centuries) based in [Kannur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannur "Kannur").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-33) Thiruvananthapuram was known as a great center of intellectual and artistic activity at this time. [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") became the most dominant state in Kerala by defeating the powerful [Zamorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamorin "Zamorin") of [Kozhikode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Kozhikode "History of Kozhikode") in the battle of [Purakkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purakkad "Purakkad") in 1755.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-AHoT_162-34)

The temple of Vishnu reclining on Anantha, the [Sri Padmanabhaswamy temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Padmanabhaswamy_temple "Sri Padmanabhaswamy temple"), is the most recognizable and iconic landmark of the city and the district and dates back to the times of the Azhvars, and is one among the 108 shrines mentioned in their texts. In addition to the presiding deity of [Padmanabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishnu "Vishnu"), this temple contains several shrines, dedicated to [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna "Krishna"), [Narasimha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narasimha "Narasimha") and [Ayyappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayyappa "Ayyappa"). King Marthanda Varma, after his conquest of Southern Kerala upto the Aluva, submitted the kingdom to Padmanabha and took upon the title of 'Sree Padmanabhadasa', the Servant of Sree Padmanabha. The vast temple complex, with its tall [Gopuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopuram "Gopuram") decorated with detailed carvings reflected in a huge [temple tank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_tank "Temple tank"), is today a center of attraction for devotees and sightseers.

The city was the capital of the [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") state from 18th century CE until [India's independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"). The Thiruvananthapuram Municipality came into existence in 1920 as the first municipality in [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") region. After two decades, during the reign of [Sree Chithira Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sree_Chithira_Thirunal "Sree Chithira Thirunal"), Thiruvananthapuram Municipality was converted into Corporation on 30 October 1940.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-35) Consequent to the recommendations of the State Reorganization Commission, the Vilavancode subdistrict of Thiruvananthapuram was merged with [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu"), along with another three southern subdistricts, Thovala, Agastheewaram, and Kalkulam from [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") which eventually formed Tamil Nadu's [Kanyakumari district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_district "Kanyakumari district"). The state of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") came into being on 1 November 1956.

### Kilimanoor palace

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Kilimanoor palace")]

See also: [Kilimanoor palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_palace "Kilimanoor palace")

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Studiorrv.jpg/250px-Studiorrv.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Studiorrv.jpg)

Birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma with his studio in the foreground

In 1705 ([ME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_era "Malayalam era") 880) the son and two daughters of Ittammar Raja of [Parappanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanad "Parappanad") royal house (originally based at [Parappanangadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanangadi "Parappanangadi") in present-day [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district")) were adopted into the Royal house of [Venad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venad "Venad"). Ittammar Raja's sister and her sons, Rama Varma and Raghava Varma, settled in Kilimanoor and married the now adopted sisters. [Marthanda Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marthanda_Varma "Marthanda Varma"), the founder of the Kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"), was the son of Raghava Varma. The nephew[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-36) of Raghava Varma, Ravi Varma Koil Thampuran, married the sister of Marthanda Varma. Their son became known as [Dharma Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharma_Raja "Dharma Raja") Kartika Thirunnal Rama Varma.

In 1740 when an allied force,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-37) led by Dutchman Captain Hockert supporting the Deshinganadu King, attacked Venad, an army from Kilimanoor resisted and then defeated them. Although a small victory, this was the first time an Indian army had defeated a European power. In 1753, in recognition of this feat, Marthanda Varma exempted the areas controlled by the Kilimanoor palace[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-38) from taxes, and granted them autonomous status.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-39) The present palace complex was built at this time, together with the Ayyappa temple.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-40) for the family deity, _Sastha_ or Ayyapan.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[Velu Thampi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velu_Thampi_Dalawa "Velu Thampi Dalawa")[Dalawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewan "Dewan") held meetings at Kilimanoor palace while planning uprisings against the British. He handed over his sword at the palace before going into his final battle against the British, and India's first President, Dr [Rajendra Prasad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajendra_Prasad "Rajendra Prasad") received this sword from the palace and it was kept in the [National Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum,_New_Delhi "National Museum, New Delhi") in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"). Afterwards the sword was moved to the Napier Museum, Thiruvananthapuram.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Climate")]

The climate of Thiruvananthapuram district is generally hot and [tropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropics "Tropics"). Large forest reserves have a favorable effect on the climate and induce rains. Cold weather is experienced in the [mountain ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Ghats "Western Ghats"). Lower down, the weather is bracing, and generally hot in the coastal regions. The mean maximum temperature is 95°F (35°C) and the mean minimum temperature is 69°F (20°C). As the district stretches from north to south, with the [Arabian Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea") to the west, the [relative humidity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relative_humidity "Relative humidity") is generally high. It rises to about 95% during the [southwest monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon#Southwest_monsoon "Monsoon").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-42)

The total annual rainfall in the district is about 1,827.7 mm (72 in) per annum.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-43) The southwest monsoon, from June to September is the principal rainy season, during which the district receives most of its annual rainfall. The second rainy season is the [Northeast monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon#Northeast_monsoon "Monsoon"), from October to November. The district also experiences thunderstorm rains in the pre-monsoon months of April and May.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-44)

December to February are the coolest months. The average temperature drops to 69°F (20°C) in these months, generally considered India's [winter season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_India#winter "Climate of India"). The [summer season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_India#Summer "Climate of India") starts in February and continues until May. The average temperature rises to 95°F (35°C) in these months.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-45)

The media and [information technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology_in_India "Information technology in India") sectors are mainstays of Thiruvananthapuram district's economy, and other major sectors are tourism and [leisure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leisure "Leisure"), agriculture, and education. India's first animation park, the [Kinfra Animation Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinfra_Film_and_Video_Park "Kinfra Film and Video Park"), is in the district.

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Technopark_Trivandum_Ganga_and_Yamuna_Buildings.jpg/250px-Technopark_Trivandum_Ganga_and_Yamuna_Buildings.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Technopark_Trivandum_Ganga_and_Yamuna_Buildings.jpg)

A [Technopark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technopark_Kerala "Technopark Kerala") building. Technopark as of 2010 has 450,000 m 2 (4,800,000 sq ft) of built-up space, and is home to over 200 companies, employing around 30,000 professionals.

Thiruvananthapuram district has 2 central-sector, 14 state-sector, 1 co-operative-sector, 4 joint-sector, and 60 private-sector medium- and large-scale enterprises. As of 31 March 2003, [Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Industrial_Development_Corporation "Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation") (KSIDC) units employed 9,262 people, and had invested Rs. 3439.4 million.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-48) In 2002, there were 901 registered working factories, including oil mills, cashew factories, [Cotton mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton_mill "Cotton mill"), [Sawmills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawmill "Sawmill"), [printing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offset_printing "Offset printing"), rubber industrial units, chemical units, match factories, general engineering units, and automobile workshops. The Shree Mulam Thirunal Shashtiabdapoorthy Memorial Institute (S.M.S.M. Institute) in Thiruvananthapuram city is a major state government emporium marketing products of Kerala's [handicraft industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handicraft "Handicraft").

The Neyyar Irrigation Project, commissioned in 1959, irrigates an area of 116.65 km 2 (45.0 sq mi). The [Neyyar river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyar_(river) "Neyyar (river)") is the source of water for the [Neyyar reservoir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyar_Dam "Neyyar Dam"). The dam is 294.13 metres (965.0 ft) long and 50.6 metres (166.0 ft) high. The catchment draining into the reservoir, covering an area of 140 km 2 (54 sq mi) of forest, receives an annual average rainfall of about 2,260 mm (90 in) 2260 mm from the two monsoons. The total length of the main canal and its branches is 266 km (165 mi).

The district administration is headed by the [District collector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_collector "District collector"). ## Local governance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Local governance")]

Local governance in Thiruvananthapuram district is administered through a three-tier system under the Kerala Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, along with urban local bodies governed by the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994. The rural areas of the district are managed by [gram panchayats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_panchayat "Gram panchayat") at the village level, [block panchayats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panchayat_samiti "Panchayat samiti") at the intermediate level, and the [district panchayat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_council_(India) "District council (India)") at the apex. Urban areas are governed by [municipal corporations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation_(India) "Municipal corporation (India)") and [municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_council_(India) "Municipal council (India)"). Thiruvananthapuram district has one municipal corporation — the [Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation "Thiruvananthapuram Corporation") — and several municipalities, including [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara "Neyyattinkara"), [Nedumangad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedumangad "Nedumangad"), [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal"), [Varkala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varkala "Varkala"), and [Kattakada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattakada "Kattakada"). The district panchayat oversees the coordinated development of rural local bodies, while urban bodies function independently under their respective councils.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-52)

## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Politics")]

Thiruvananthapuram district sees a dynamic political landscape with major alliances led by the [Communist Party of India (Marxist)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India_(Marxist) "Communist Party of India (Marxist)") and the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"). The [Left Democratic Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left_Democratic_Front "Left Democratic Front") (LDF), led by CPI(M), and the [United Democratic Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Democratic_Front_(Kerala) "United Democratic Front (Kerala)") (UDF), led by Congress, dominate the scene, alongside the [National Democratic Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Alliance "National Democratic Alliance") (NDA), led by the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party"). In the 2019 General Election, both Thiruvananthapuram and Attingal parliamentary constituencies in the Thiruvananthapuram district were won by the Indian National Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF). In the 2021 Assembly Election, the Left Democratic Front (LDF) secured an impressive victory by winning 13 out of the total 14 seats in the Thiruvananthapuram district.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-53)

## Transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_district&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Transport")]

Main article: [Transport in Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_in_Thiruvananthapuram "Transport in Thiruvananthapuram")

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Lulumalltrivandrum.jpg/250px-Lulumalltrivandrum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lulumalltrivandrum.jpg)

A highway at [Akkulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akkulam "Akkulam") in Thiruvananthapuram

National Highway 66 (formerly known as [National Highway 47](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_47_(India) "National Highway 47 (India)")) stretches from Kaliyikkavila at its southern end to [Navaikulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navaikulam "Navaikulam") near [Parippally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parippally "Parippally") in the north, covering a distance of 80 km (50 mi) within the district.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-58) The [Main Central Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Central_Road "Main Central Road") covers a distance of 55 km (34 mi), passing through [Kesavadasapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kesavadasapuram "Kesavadasapuram"), [Vembayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vembayam "Vembayam"), [Venjaramoodu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venjaramoodu "Venjaramoodu"), [Kilimanoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor "Kilimanoor"), and [Nilamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilamel "Nilamel") in the north. The [Kerala Public Works Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Public_Works_Department "Kerala Public Works Department") maintains some 1,552 km (964 mi) of road in the district. Local bodies are responsible for the maintenance of 9,500 km (5,900 mi) of road. There are 116 bridges in Thiruvananthapuram District.

Rail transport in the district is operated by [Southern Railway zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Railway_Zone_(India) "Southern Railway Zone (India)") of [Indian Railways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Railways "Indian Railways"). Thiruvananthapuram is connected to the rest of the country by [broad gauge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broad_gauge "Broad gauge") railway line. 82 km (51 mi) of railway line passes through the district.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district#cite_note-59) Thiruvananthapuram district currently has 20 stations, including [Thiruvananthapuram Central railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Central_railway_station "Thiruvananthapuram Central railway station").

Domestic and international airlines operate from [Thiruvananthapuram International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_International_Airport "Thiruvananthapuram International Airport"), which has direct flights to many international cities, including [Kuwait City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait_City "Kuwait City"), [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai"), [Dammam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dammam "Dammam"), [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore"), [Malé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mal%C3%A9 "Malé"), [Colombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombo "Colombo"), [Sharjah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharjah_(city) "Sharjah (city)"), [Muscat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscat,_Oman "Muscat, Oman"), [Manama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manama "Manama"), [Doha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doha "Doha"), [Jeddah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeddah "Jeddah"), and [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi"). Domestic flights link it with [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai"), [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"), [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"), [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad,_India "Hyderabad, India"), [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore"), and [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata").
